channel.title: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?"

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: My theory: 173 was originally created as a guardian totem to keep 682 in place, like a scarecrow. I believe 682 has spent much of it's existence contained by the Jailors in one form or another, and 173 was one of it's first guardians from when early Jailors couldn't manage to keep someone watching 682 and made something to keep watch when mortals failed. Just stop to think about what 173 had to be in order to hold 682 if that's what it was made for, an when it was perfected, it scared 682 because that's why it really exists. It kills everything because it wants to kill 682 and will kill anything that gets in it's way.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: 682 is Kato's big fan, and aware that damage the statue won't end well for us.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: The go to answer is that 682 comprehends 173’s true form and want to stay as far away from it as fucking possible.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded:
It does seem odd that 682 adapts to non existence but not acid, but remember that water bears can survive exposure to outer space but not being eaten by snails.

I think 682 evolved regeneration as a general catch-all way to not die and only manifests additional abilities when the regeneration is insufficient to prevent death. It doesn’t need acid resistance to avoid being killed by the acid, since its regeneration is enough to keep it alive already. To recover from getting chucked into the void, it has to come up with something more creative than that. 682 isn’t an unstoppable Doomsday-like juggernaut that adapts to everything to make itself more powerful; rather, it operates on similar principles to real animals and only adapts as necessary to survive.

As for why 682 doesn’t kill 173, that’s not just because it’s a sacred cow. 682’s reaction implies all sorts of horrible things about 173. Just think: Why, in universe, wouldn’t 682 destroy the statue? What does it know that we don’t? This the is the uncomfortable question the author wanted you to ask yourself when you read that.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: 682 is never going to be killed in the test log. That's the appeal, figuring out why the attempt doesn't work.

item.content:encoded: i just dont trust the logs at all because of how much they dont make sense to me, like the dude adapts to literal non-existence, yet doesnt seem to adapt to the acid in his cell. id say the only reason would be because 173 is the original, no other reason, 682 would probably just destroy 173 in reality, or just not care since 173 wouldnt be able to kill him

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded:
In the log, 173 was able to tear apart 682, where SCP-682 was able to survive only because 173 was unable to reach far enough to kill him.

So in my opinion, 173 is very powerful and had to be nerfed by some other god thing, and that's why 682 fears 173.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded:
It snaps your neck when you aren't looking, weren't you paying attention?

More seriously: To me, test logs like that make it a whole lot cooler. While I'm grateful to 173 for starting the site, it really isn't much by today's standards, and test logs tend to imply narrative where one is sorely lacking. The idea that 173 is much more than the Foundation describes just makes the first entry that much more enjoyable. :)
Not everyone likes the test logs, though, and many don't count them in their head-canon.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: In my canon, 173 is something far more sinister and powerful than anything contained. 682 just saw wants under the stone prison with its sight (implied to be drastically different than human sight), and saw it's true form.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: It also subtly implies something much greater about 173/much lesser about 682 than is in their original articles, which works great for getting the mind thinking.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: The meta reason is that test logs where something actually kills 682 for good aren't narratively possible, and logs where nothing happens are boring. 682 almost dying and being scared is a more satisfying outcome.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded:
For one, SCP-682 is definitely not the most powerful scip (at least, in my headcanon its not).

The same question could be asked towards anyone and a fear of bugs. Why do we fear wasps when we are very obviously more powerful then them? It's because they can cause immense pain, as SCP-173 can to SCP-682.

Yes, SCP-173 has failed to terminate SCP-682, but it got fairly damn close. That's much more powerful than a wasp is in my previous analogy. We are the reptile, SCP-173 is the wasp.

That's my way of explaining it.

item.title: Re: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded:
I mean, that's pretty intimidating spray-paint.

Serious answer: There's no canon, so take separate test logs with a grain of salt, especially collaborations.

item.title: Why does SCP-682 fear SCP-173?
item.content:encoded: I would like to know why SCP-682, the most powerful SCP in the SCP Foundation, fears SCP-173?
